sentences.text: Acronemus was a small animal that grew to be between 30 and 35 centimeters long.
Fossil evidence showed that teeth originally named Acrodus bicarinatus and fin spines named Nemacanthus tuberculatus belonged to the same animal, leading to the name Acronemus tuberculatus.
Acronemus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Acronemus belongs to the parent group Euselachii.
Acronemus is classified as Euselachii incertae sedis because it possesses a mix of features resembling both hybodontiforms and neoselachians.
A 2018 study suggested Acronemus belongs to the family Tristychiidae and is closely related to the genus Tristychius.
Acronemus lived during the Middle Triassic period in Switzerland.
Fossils of Acronemus are found in the Anisian-age Grenzbitumenzone, also known as the Besano Formation, at Monte San Giorgio.
